title: Dad fined after son, 2, died in Cyprus hotel fall
summary: Joshua Foster will have to pay 3,000 euro (£2,500), a judge in Paphos rules.

blocks.text: A father whose two-year-old boy fell to his death at a five-star hotel in Cyprus has been fined 3,000 euro (£2,500).
Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed the boy on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and "lost control" of him, Paphos District Court previously heard.
The boy fell nearly 40ft (12.1m) from the fourth floor of the King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort on 12 July, the first day of the family's holiday in Chlorakas.
Foster, 37, from Essex, admitted causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act and was sentenced on Friday morning.
He told reporters afterwards: "Thank you for the support. I'm looking forward to going home and being with my wife and daughter."
The auditor, his wife, two children and in-laws had arrived in Cyprus in the early hours of the morning on the date of the incident.
They spent the day carrying out various activities, including visiting the pool, before getting ready for dinner in the evening.
At about 18:00, Foster, his father-in-law and son walked towards an elevator, and his lawyer, Alexandros Alexandrou, told the court he was in a "good mood" and was playing with his son.
